title: Ask the Peers: Ranking NFR Coverage Gaps for Requirements Review
abstract: arXiv:2611.23296v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Missing or underrepresented non-functional requirements (NFR) categories leave little direct evidence in a requirements set, making them difficult to identify during requirements review. In this study, we frame NFR coverage-gap review as a project-level ranking task: given a target requirements specification, the goal is to rank the 11 PROMISE NFR categories for analyst inspection. We compare seven statistical, embedding-based, and large language model (LLM)-based configurations that differ in both ranking mechanism and evidence source, including target requirement statements, peer requirements, their semantic representation, and peer category statistics. We evaluate the configurations using controlled gap injection with leave-one-project-out evaluation on PROMISE, PROMISE+, PURE-Transport, and PURE-Business. translated_title: 询问同行：为需求评审排序NFR覆盖缺口
translated_abstract: 缺失或代表性不足的非功能需求（NFR）类别在需求集合中留下的直接证据很少，使得这些类别在需求评审过程中难以识别。在本研究中，我们将NFR覆盖缺口评审构建为一个项目级排序任务：给定一个目标需求规格说明，目标是对11个PROMISE NFR类别进行排序，以供分析师检查。我们比较了七种基于统计、基于嵌入和基于大语言模型（LLM）的配置，它们在排序机制和证据来源上各不相同，证据来源包括目标需求陈述、同行需求、其语义表示以及同行类别统计。我们采用受控缺口注入和留一项目交叉评估方法，在PROMISE、PROMISE+、PURE-Transport和PURE-Business数据集上对这些配置进行评估。使用同行类别统计的四种配置在完全移除场景下表现基本持平（平均AUROC为0.875-0.889）……
tldr: 本研究将NFR覆盖缺口评审建模为项目级排序任务，实验表明利用同行项目类别统计信息的四种配置表现最优且效果相近（平均AUROC达0.875-0.889）。
en_tdlr: This study frames NFR coverage-gap review as a project-level ranking task, showing that four configurations leveraging peer category statistics achieve the best and comparable performance (mean AUROC 0.875-0.889) across multiple datasets.
